core.title: Feedback-loop features must close the loop in smoke
core.given: A feature is marked as a feedback-loop feature (its kind declaration says so).
core.when: The planner authors or revises the feature's plan items and their smoke acceptances.
core.then: At least one smoke acceptance must declare a close_the_loop block carrying both consumer_reacted (the consumer-side assertion the test makes) and drift_resolved (the convergence assertion).
prefer: Add (or extend) a smoke acceptance on the feature's primary plan item with a close_the_loop block declaring consumer_reacted and drift_resolved.
Phrase them so the test asserts the consumer actually received the correction and a producer re-run yields 0 new corrections for the same drift.
avoid: Producer-only smoke assertions (artifact existence, schema validation) as the sole smoke coverage.
A close_the_loop block with only one of the two keys.
consumer_reacted satisfied by a fake send-history.
unless: The feature's kind declaration carries this rule's dated suppression marker (the stack's time-boxed suppression syntax) — dated, so the debt expires; an expired marker no longer suppresses.
core.why: Producer-only smoke assertions give false-positive green CI while the loop's consumer end is never exercised.
evidence: Every feature marked feedback-loop has at least one smoke acceptance whose acceptance block contains a close_the_loop block with both consumer_reacted and drift_resolved keys.
The corresponding test asserts real consumer receipt of the correction (not a fake send-history) and that a producer re-run yields 0 new corrections for the same drift.
Otherwise, the feature's kind declaration carries this rule's suppression marker with an expiry date not yet passed.
verification: Presence check over the plan artifacts: trigger on a feature whose kind declaration marks it feedback-loop; pass iff at least one of its smoke acceptances has a close_the_loop block containing both consumer_reacted and drift_resolved. The check verifies declaration presence only — it does not verify that the implementing test really asserts consumer receipt and convergence (that test-implementation obligation is split to a separate tester-facing rule, as in the reference realization).

Suppression: a dated suppression marker placed on the feature's kind declaration, using the stack's suppression-marker syntax (profile enforcement.suppression_marker); the debt expires on the given date — an expired marker no longer suppresses.

values: smoke acceptance added or edited on a feedback-loop feature
feedback-loop feature with no smoke acceptance whose close_the_loop block carries both consumer_reacted and drift_resolved

fires: The planner authors or edits a feature marked feedback-loop and its smoke acceptances.
A feedback-loop feature's only smoke acceptances assert artifact existence or schema validity of the producer output.
No smoke acceptance on a feedback-loop feature has a close_the_loop block carrying both consumer_reacted and drift_resolved (e.g. the only close_the_loop blocks each miss one of the keys).
doesNotFire: Features whose kind is not feedback-loop.

A feedback-loop feature where at least one smoke acceptance has a close_the_loop block with both consumer_reacted and drift_resolved, even if other smoke or non-smoke acceptances lack such a block or carry an incomplete one.
A feedback-loop feature whose kind declaration carries an unexpired dated suppression of this rule.

neutralityNotes: close_the_loop, consumer_reacted and drift_resolved are kept verbatim in the core: they are the acceptance-content schema of the ATDD methodology itself (this convention's own subject matter, cf. term close_the_loop_block), not stack machinery, so every realization of the rule shares them. 'smoke' is kept as the neutral acceptance tier (the profile vocabulary already knows urn.smoke_acceptance); bun.json never states how an acceptance is marked smoke-tier, so that marking mechanism stays with each realization. The concrete artifact names (feature YAML, DESIRED OUTCOME YAML, acceptance YAML) come from roles.plan_artifact.kinds, and the kind-line syntax from the proposed key idiom.plan_syntax#feature_kind_declaration. Per-rule disposition (suppress-and-clean) and severity (3) live in core verification; the detector/validator id is bunOnly. The presence check covers declaration presence only; the real-assertion obligation (no fake send-history, producer re-run yields 0 new corrections) remains a separate tester-facing rule exactly as in bun.json's splitSuggestion, and the core's verification records that boundary. No roots or exclusion deference appears in bun.json, so none is asserted.
